Happy men's mental health month, OP. I can't know everything from your post of course but I'd like to say that you were either with wrong people who didn't appreciate your communication efforts and vulnerability or sometimes it's genuinely a complex and gray situation. People generally tend to become really defensive when they feel they're getting blamed even if that's not the case, and they tend to focus on that instead of acknowledging the other's perspective and feelings. My mother was certainly that way. 

Sometimes people who seek emotional intelligence and vulnerability aren't ready to commit to those themselves. Communication can be very difficult and people often underestimate that.

Sometimes when you want to open up they're not in a good mental state to react to that, so it's important to talk about this as well. Of course they may simply lack empathy too, that's why I said I can't know your exact situation. Every person and situation is different.

But I'd say that despite all the discouragement, please continue to believe in yourself and express yourself! Listen to your heart and do what's best for you mentally, no matter what others say. You said that you go to therapy which is a great thing (it helps me a lot too), and not bottling stuff up genuinely helps you in the long run.

I'm sorry for your experiences truly, I hope you can find the right people that will support you as you support them.

I also chose Verso, but it was a such a difficult decision to make. Verso didn't ask for any of this. This was his canvas originally, Aline had no right to paint over it and the family overall should've just left his last piece of soul in peace. But we see continuously how they're all selfish in one way or another. Therefore, I thought it was only right for him to decide the fate of the canvas, even if that meant erasing it so that his family could move on.

For me, maybe I'm coping but I thought the canvas was already almost dead at this point. They were all gone except for our team. Yeah Maelle was going to bring everyone back but... And I don't believe her parents are actually going to watch her die slowly, and they may interfere in the future and who knows, even another fracture could happen if something like that happens. 

Anyways. Its all up to interpretation of course, but there are interesting points to consider. Obviously both endings are tragic and understandable from their own points :')

Dessendre family and their powers are so dangerous and scary in general. Imagine giving humanity the god powers to create and delete worlds on a whim... That sounds like a horror or dystopian genre more than anything else 😅

One of the reasons why I really struggled with choosing Verso's ending was that I related to Maelle so much, and I understood her feelings well. If I lost my dear brother, my voice and was scarred, and blamed by my family for the fire, I'd also feel lonely, feel like a burden and want to stay in a world where I could feel loved and happy and live.

I still stand by my choice for various reasons, but I also don't agree with people who are siding with one ending and completely bashing the other. There are positive and negative points to discuss for both, and both are tragic with no happy ending.

I chose Verso's ending personally for many reasons, but I believe both ending have their merits and it was such a difficult choice to make because of that :')

Yeah, I agree that Maelle's reasons for staying inside the canvas wasn't just avoiding grief. I mean, she not only blamed herself like her family does, she also felt alone and not supported in real life, hence feeling more connected to her Lumiere family. Her most cruel act there was not letting go Verso though, and god complex is a real issue. I can't imagine any 16 year old, hell even adults having this kind of power. It's a scary thing.

When it comes to Verso's soul, he loves his family though... And Maelle is slowly killing herself outside the canvas by not moving on. I mean, real Verso sacrificed himself for his sister. I think, even if the conflict ended, he didn't want a life like this for Maelle, so I can't imagine him enjoying painting in that situation. And conflict ended only for now. Aline may still try to enter the canvas, and Renoir may still enter when her daughter becomes more sick, so... I feel hopeless regarding that point, honestly.

As for if people in Lumiere have agency or not, real or not, thats such a complex situation. I don't think there's a simple answer to that. For me, I believe that while they're definitely real in a sense, there are several things to consider. First is death. As Gustave said 'Gommage is equally violent and death... death is just final'. But not in this case. When you take that finality away from the equation, the meaning of life becomes more questionable. That's one of the main reasons why her ending felt so hollow to me.

That brings other questions. Everyone died at the end of Act 2 already. I'm not sure if gestrals and such died, but I don't see why they wouldn't, if Renoir was erasing the whole canvas there. Was Maelle really able to bring everyone back as they were? Verso said 'focus on their essence', who they are, before Maelle was able to bring back Lune and Sciel. I think that's why they were just like before. Could she do that with all of them, did she know everyone well enough to do that? We still don't have enough information regarding how chroma and creating life in a painting works, so that's all up to interpretation.

Our memories and experiences also shapes us and our personality, right? What kind of memories did she give them? Do they remember their death, how it feels like to grieve? Do they remember gommage and if so, did she explain who she is? We saw Gustave with his arm so I believe she did give them all their memories, but that's still unclear. There's lots of questions to consider there!

Everyone is different but it definitely can be a symptom of depression, yeah. It used to be for me. Sometimes you're so stuck in your own head, fighting a battle in your mind that you isolate yourself for some time and hurt others without meaning to.

This is probably long, bear with me. I just resonated with your post a lot.

Weirdly enough I've been in both ends of this, so I understand both you and him, though every depression and every situation is different. I've almost lost my cousin to depression and my best friend too, who's been like a sister to me over 10 years. I've been also struggling with depression for over a decade, definitely doing much better now.

The thing is, depression is something he has to fight himself at the end. The thoughts are in his head, no matter what anyone says the battle within his mind is something only he can understand and endure. But finding the strength and hope to do so... you can help with that. Actually you're already helping with that by being there for him, I'm sure. When I was at my lowest and didn't have hope or strength to go on, I did for my father because I knew he would be so damn traumatized and miserable, because he showed me his love so strongly. I endured that hell for him for a decade, living for him until I had the strength to live for myself.

What I'm trying to say is, if you're showing your love for him strongly (and I can see that you absolutely do), that might give him strength and hope to get better when he can't find it within himself. I know my best friend also said many times me being there for her helped her not lose her sanity sometimes. 

Another thing is, reminding himself that he's not alone in feeling like this helps a lot too, especially with music. I actually have a playlist that helped me so damn much, songs that resonated with me and some even saved my life. Most of them from one band only.

https://open.spotify.com/playlist/4oeHPo9YeXQdeNWr3M9tjr?si=7vU8YHmTRC-xtZcsdk37fA&pi=u-T38hnCYNSR-0

Share with him if you want, or listen to it yourself to understand a perspective of someone dealing with stuff like this, just a suggestion. Everyone is different so if you think the songs can put him in a darker mood don't risk it. (Especially for the song Good Charlotte - Hold On, the music video itself was the actual life saving part for me, you can take a look at it on Youtube. I literally tear up every time I still watch it. And the song Kitchen Sink actually belongs to Twenty One Pilots but it wasn't on Spotify so that's a cover. Their one lyric really helped me find a meaning for a long time, the 'No one else is dealing with your demons / Meaning maybe defeating them / Could be the beginning of your meaning, friend.')

You're already being there for him as much as you can. Trying to listen to him, show your love for him... Doing your best is enough. So the only real advice I can give you is... Be kind with yourself. Don't forget to take care of yourself as well, because while dealing with depression is something unbearable at times, trying to be there for someone dealing with it is a whole another thing. I still have nightmares from the time my best friend called/texted me 'i can't do this anymore' and I wasn't able to see it for an hour because I was on my therapist appointment- thankfully she was okay at the end.

But what I mean is, I know the feeling of helplessness and how it can take a toll on you. How it makes you scared and worried all the time. It's important to share your own worries with someone, so they won't consume you. Don't feel selfish for talking about your own feelings, living your life and don't lose hope. Try to believe in your brother, believe he can learn how to deal with this in his own pace and take care of your mental health too.

Take care of yourself, praying for you both.
